investigation_notes:
Current state: **healthy - no ongoing cause for upload failure found**

Evidence:

- Both containers `running`: app `Up 24 minutes`, db `Up 2 minutes (healthy)` (E1).
- App details: `running:true, exit_code:0, oom_killed:false, restart_count:0`, started `2026-10-28T16:35:11Z` (E4).
- DB details: `running:true, exit_code:0, oom_killed:false, health:healthy`, started `2026-10-28T16:57:17Z` (E8).
- `/health` now `200 {"status":"ok"}` (E2) and log `GET /health 200 OK` at `16:59:26` (E11).
- Most recent upload in logs succeeded: `POST /upload 200 OK` at `16:57:23` + `GET /files/ef77... 200 OK` (E11). Earlier upload at `16:52:20 POST /upload 200 OK` + `GET /files/bd2d... 200 OK` also succeeded (E5, E11).
- Storage for uploads present: bind `source:/srv/lab-data destination:/data rw:true` (E4), on same network `incidentlab_default` for both app (E4) and db (E8).
- Space is available now: `/srv/lab-data 8.0% used, 415.2 MB available, inode 0.2%` (E6) and `/ 6.4% used, inode 1.4%` (E10).
- Upload directory writable by app user: `owner 1000:1000 mode 0755, app_uid 1000, app_user_can_write:true` (E7).

Historical failures seen in logs, both now resolved:

- `16:46:12 File "/app/main.py", line 58, in upload out.write(chunk) OSError: [Errno 28] No space left on device` (E5, E11). Ruled out as ongoing by current space (E6, E10).
- `16:52:23 health check failed ... psycopg.OperationalError: failed to resolve host 'db': Temporary failure in name resolution` leading to `GET /health 503` (E5, E11). Correlates with DB `received fast shutdown request` at `16:52:20.582` + `database system is shut down` (E9) and DB `finished_at:2026-10-28T16:52:20` then restart `started_at:2026-10-28T16:57:17` (E8). DB is now `healthy` (E8) and `/health 200` (E2, E11), so dependency outage resolved.
- DB logs show repeated `received fast shutdown request` / `database system is ready to accept connections` cycles at `16:43:58, 16:44:05, 16:44:11, 16:52:20` and restart at `16:57:17` (E9).

Conclusion: report of stopped uploads matches past transient errors - disk write error and DB-down period causing health 503 - but latest evidence shows uploads and health succeeding with resources available. No actionable ongoing root cause. 12/12 checks used.
